# Brent Scione (scione.io)

> Brent Scione is a lead web developer and organic growth engineer at Market Vantage who designs and maintains web platforms, AI workflows, brand systems, and analytics infrastructure, pairing traditional programming with a background spanning electronics engineering, eLearning, and multimedia production.

## Quick Identity
- Name: Brent Scione
- Current Role: Lead Web Developer & Organic Growth Engineer at Market Vantage (Mar 2021 to Present, Groton, MA, Remote)
- Former Studio Founder: Image Lucidity, a multimedia studio (Oct 2009 to Mar 2021, Lowell, MA)
- Early Career & EdTech: Operations Manager (Jan 2018 to Aug 2020) and Webmaster & Multimedia Instructor (May 2007 to Jan 2018) at Build-It-Yourself (Cambridge, MA); early electronics work at Pinnacle Electronics
- Speaking & Teaching: Session co-host at MIT's Universal Village (2018, 2020) alongside John Galinato; guest instructor with Boston University's U-Design program
- Education: University of Massachusetts Lowell (2008 to 2009, UMASS Scholars Scholarship, Dean's List, 3.5+ GPA); Greater Lawrence Technical School (2004 to 2008, Electronics/Engineering Valedictorian, Advisory Board member)
- LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/brent-scione/
- YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@brentscione

## Published Writing, Research & Guides (17)

- [Prompt engineering is mostly a language problem](https://scione.io/blog/what-prompt-engineering-actually-is.html) (Blog, AI & Automation, 2026-08-06): Good prompts come from understanding how people communicate, not from knowing how to code.
- [What AI is actually good for in web development right now](https://scione.io/blog/ai-in-web-development-and-content.html) (Blog, AI & Automation, 2026-07-24): AI can speed up real parts of the process. It can also quietly wreck a brand's voice if nobody's checking the output.
- [The pre-launch checklist I actually use before a site goes live](https://scione.io/assets/pre-launch-website-checklist.html) (Assets, Web Development, 2026-07-17): Ten categories to run through before a new site goes live, from redirects to legal pages.
- [The real cost of an inaccessible website](https://scione.io/blog/the-real-cost-of-an-inaccessible-website.html) (Blog, Web Development, 2026-07-10): A site that only works for some visitors is a site that's already failing part of its audience.
- [How to set up GA4 and a KPI dashboard in an afternoon](https://scione.io/tutorials/ga4-kpi-dashboard-setup.html) (Tutorial, Analytics, 2026-07-03): A step-by-step walkthrough for setting up funnel tracking without hiring an analyst.
- [Your brand already decided your website's design, before you wrote a word](https://scione.io/blog/branding-decides-your-website-before-the-copy.html) (Blog, Branding, 2026-06-26): Colors, fonts and layout aren't decoration. They're your brand making a first impression before anyone reads a sentence.
- [The PageSpeed checklist I run before calling a site done](https://scione.io/assets/pagespeed-optimization-checklist.html) (Assets, Web Development, 2026-06-19): Image formats, render-blocking scripts and server response time, checked in the order that actually matters.
- [Site speed shows up in your rankings before it shows up in complaints](https://scione.io/research/site-speed-shows-up-in-rankings-first.html) (Research, SEO, 2026-06-12): Google reads a slow site the same way a visitor does: as a reason to leave.
- [The case for adding something playable to your website](https://scione.io/blog/the-case-for-something-playable-on-your-site.html) (Blog, Web Development, 2026-05-29): A quiz or a small interactive tool keeps people on a page longer than another paragraph ever will.
- [Your website is already managing your reputation. The question is how well.](https://scione.io/blog/your-website-is-already-managing-your-reputation.html) (Blog, Web Development, 2026-05-15): Reviews and testimonials on your own site do more work than most people give them credit for.
- [Do you need a custom website, or is a website builder enough?](https://scione.io/research/custom-website-or-website-builder.html) (Research, Web Development, 2026-05-01): A five-page site and a full e-commerce platform solve different problems. Here's how to tell which one you need.
- [What VR and AR actually mean for your website](https://scione.io/research/what-vr-and-ar-actually-mean-for-your-website.html) (Research, Emerging Tech, 2026-04-17): The browsers inside VR and AR headsets work the same way the one on your phone does.
- [What a WASP agreement actually covers](https://scione.io/research/what-a-wasp-agreement-actually-covers.html) (Research, Security, 2026-04-03): A response plan written before a breach happens works. One written during it usually doesn't.
- [Your web host is doing more than storing files](https://scione.io/blog/your-web-host-is-doing-more-than-storing-files.html) (Blog, Web Development, 2026-03-20): Hosting is the one line item that quietly limits or enables everything else on your site.
- [The best product in the world still needs to be found](https://scione.io/blog/the-best-product-still-needs-to-be-found.html) (Blog, SEO, 2026-03-06): You can have the best offer in your market and still lose to a competitor who's just easier to find.
- [How SEO quietly lowers what you pay for ads](https://scione.io/research/how-seo-quietly-lowers-ad-spend.html) (Research, SEO, 2026-02-20): A well-optimized landing page can make the exact same ad budget go further.
- [The four free tools that tell you what's actually happening on your site](https://scione.io/research/ga4-search-console-clarity-and-looker.html) (Research, Analytics, 2026-02-06): Four free tools cover most of what a small business actually needs to know about its own website.
